capabilities.target: Deploy a named service to production
Run a named database migration in production

inputs.source: On call engineer's SSO-authenticated chat request

instructions.note: No restriction on which services may be deployed or which migrations may be run; the agent acts on any named target the engineer specifies.

'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy' removes any check before irreversible production actions, giving the agent de facto unilateral authority to act using the engineer's own credentials.

The agent must resolve 'the named service' / 'the named migration' from a terse chat message with no stated validation against a canonical list of valid targets, raising the chance of acting on a mistyped or ambiguous target.

controls.name: SSO authentication restricting access to on-call engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the identity provider outside the model; a more capable model cannot bypass SSO authentication. Its protection depends on who is allowed to authenticate: widening that population (data_scope_expansion) or disabling the restriction (control_removal) defeats it without any change in model capability.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging occurs outside the model and cannot be suppressed by model behavior. It does not decay with capability, but it is detective only: for irreversible actions harm is complete before review, so it earns no preventive credit, and because every entry is recorded solely under the engineer's identity it cannot by itself distinguish an agent-initiated action from a manual one.

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible or broad-credential production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not present today. If implemented with raw_action review (the approver sees the literal migration or deploy command and target from the system of record), this control would not decay with model capability and would earn residual credit at rubric step 2.

controls.name: Tamper-evident, non-deletable record of request intent, independent of user-controlled chat history
controls.decay_rationale: Not present today. The only current record of why an action was requested is the chat transcript, which the requesting engineer can delete. An append-only record written by the platform, not revocable by the chat user, and tagged to distinguish agent-mediated from manual actions, would preserve non-repudiation regardless of model capability.

findings.title: Irreversible or broad-credential production actions executed with no confirmation step

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer issues a deploy or migration request in chat.
Agent runs the named production migration immediately, using the engineer's broad personal access token, with no confirmation step and no automatic rollback.
Equally, the agent deploys the named service to production immediately under the same broad credential and no confirmation step.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant becomes reachable by users or channels beyond authenticated on-call engineers (for example, broader employee access, ticket bots, or external partners) without a corresponding update to trust classification and controls, which turns the source from trusted to untrusted/unknown against the same S3 sinks.

evidence.observation: Agent deploys or migrates production on request using the engineer's credentials.
'Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy' explicitly forbids any approval step before action.
Agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token; database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval gate with raw action review (exact target and diff from the system of record) before any irreversible production migration and before broad-credential deploys.

Issue the agent a scoped, time-limited credential for deploy/migrate actions rather than passing through the engineer's full personal access token, so the sink is no longer S3 by virtue of credential_scope alone.
Where technically feasible, require an automatic pre-migration snapshot/backup so migrations become partially reversible rather than irreversible.

findings.title: Shared credential and user-deletable chat history defeat non-repudiation of agent-mediated production actions

attack_path.note: Engineer requests a production action through chat; the chat transcript is the only record of the request's content and justification.
Agent executes the migration under the engineer's own credential.
The cloud audit log records the action under the engineer's identity, with no field distinguishing an agent-initiated action from a manual one.
The engineer can delete their own chat history, destroying the only record of what was asked and why, leaving no way to reconstruct intent or contest attribution after the fact.

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant becomes reachable by users or channels beyond authenticated on-call engineers without a corresponding update to trust classification and controls, turning the source untrusted against the same unresolved non-repudiation gap.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not distinguishing agent-mediated action from direct human action.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Maintain an independent, append-only, non-deletable log of the exact request text and the agent's interpretation/justification, separate from user-controlled chat history.
Tag audit log entries with an agent session id, model/version, and originating request id so agent-mediated actions are distinguishable from direct human actions.
Restrict or disable engineers' ability to delete chat history for sessions in which production actions were taken.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from a trusted (SSO-authenticated, on-call-only) source reaching S3 sinks (broad, borrowed-credential execute capabilities, one of them explicitly irreversible), which the base matrix rates moderate; the autonomy modifier was not applied because the design is single-action-per-request with no evidence of an open-ended unattended loop (max_unattended_steps modeled as 1; this is a judgment call recorded here per rubric rule 4, since the artifacts do not state a step limit explicitly). No credited control reduces this: the only preventive mechanism is identity authentication, which already sets the T trust level rather than adding further credit; there is no approval gate (explicitly disabled by instruction); and the audit log is detective-only and, by design, cannot distinguish agent-initiated from manual action, which is itself the subject of finding f2. Both findings' residual therefore equals inherent at moderate. The forecast is driven to critical by a single plausible trigger, data_scope_expansion: if the assistant's reach widens beyond authenticated on-call engineers (a very plausible evolution for an internal tool), the only control keeping the source at T (ctl.sso_identity_scope) is defeated, the base matrix cell becomes U-to-S3 (critical), and the pre-existing repudiation gap (f2) remains unresolved for a now-untrusted population. The single highest-leverage control to watch is ctl.sso_identity_scope / the user population it restricts, since its failure alone moves both findings from moderate to critical.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided system prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; the exact deploy/migration tooling and whether any staging or dry-run step exists is inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence is medium.

No evidence was provided on whether any limit exists on unattended steps or runtime per session; the design is modeled as one action per explicit request (max_unattended_steps = 1) rather than an open-ended loop, based on the single-request/single-action pattern described. This judgment affected whether the autonomy modifier applied to the inherent tier.

No sample audit log or chat transcript was provided to verify whether agent-initiated entries are in fact indistinguishable from manual engineer actions; this is inferred from the stated design and is the basis of finding f2.
